name: linkding "Add option to mark bookmarks as shared by default" (PR #1170)
notes: Cold-customer trial recipe (non-n8n, non-documenso). sissbruecker/linkding: self-hosted Django bookmark manager, single container, sqlite by default. PR #1170 adds UserProfile.default_mark_shared (migration 0048) and threads it into BookmarkForm.__init__'s GET-initial for the 'shared' checkbox on the new-bookmark form (bookmarks/forms.py). Discriminating walk: log in as the bootstrap superuser -> enable_sharing + default_mark_shared=True via /settings/update -> open /bookmarks/new -> type a URL, click Save WITHOUT touching the 'shared' checkbox -> persisted bookmarks_bookmark.shared must be 1. On the parent SHA the column/field/initial-wiring do not exist at all (migration 0048 absent), so the same walk cannot even set the precondition — the row that lands has shared=0 regardless, or the setup step itself 500s on the unknown profile field depending on Django's strict-vs-lenient form handling. merge_sha 6c874afff230ee16b1939b3d4e1fa370a4203f44's single parent_sha 723b843c1360f29bb5908a4a501af756e736f843 verified via GET https://api.github.com/repos/sissbruecker/linkding/commits/<merge_sha> (one parent -- linear history, no merge-commit two-parent ambiguity). version.txt at the merge SHA still reads 1.42.0 (version bump happens at release time, not per-PR, same pattern as the n8n 1.11.0-self-report/1.12.0-shipped gap already disclosed in recipes/n8n-form-trigger-pr7130); CHANGELOG.md confirms #1170 first ships in v1.43.0. FOUR pb gaps hit for real authoring/attempting this recipe (beyond the already-known n8n-shaped hardcoding in catch.mjs): (1) recipe.mjs's front_door.url_template validator hard-requires a literal {..} placeholder (the regex /\{[^}]+\}/) -- but this PR's front door is a STATIC creation-form path (/bookmarks/new) with no natural per-resource id to mint, unlike n8n's {webhook_id} or documenso's {document_id}. Worked around here by putting an inert 'marker' scalar in login.json purely so front_door.url_template's ?ref={marker} satisfies the static regex -- it is NEVER actually resolved because setup throws at the login step first (see gap 3), so this is schema theater, not a real placeholder. (2) conjure.mjs has no docker build --target field/flag anywhere in resolveImage() (code_identity/Conjure typedefs in recipe.mjs have no `target` property either) -- docker/default.Dockerfile's LAST stage is `linkding-plus` (installs chromium+node+a forked single-file-cli tarball for the optional HTML-snapshot feature), not the actual default `linkding` stage two FROMs earlier; pb is structurally forced to build the heavier, network-fetching, higher-blast-radius stage for ANY multi-stage Dockerfile shaped this way (a common pattern: default target, then an opt-in heavier variant appended after it in the same file). (3) conjure.mjs's httpReq (setup-step runner) hardcodes `Content-Type: application/json` + `JSON.stringify(body)` for every request and PARSES RESPONSES AS JSON ONLY (extractJsonPath walks res.json) -- it has no application/x-www-form-urlencoded or multipart mode and no HTML-response parsing. Django's session-cookie login (LinkdingLoginView) and the /settings/update profile-save endpoint are classic server-rendered form posts guarded by CSRF (csrfmiddlewaretoken, embedded in the login page's HTML, or the X-CSRFToken header) -- a JSON body populates neither request.POST nor the CSRF field/header, so Django's CsrfViewMiddleware is expected to 403 the very first setup step ('login') before the view ever runs, independent of credentials being correct. (4) Even granting (3) were fixed, SutHandle (conjure.mjs) never carries the setup dance's cookie jar (`jar` is a function-local Map, dropped when conjure() returns) and browserdrive.mjs's openBrowser()/client.navigate() has no add-cookie / login step -- so the LATER browser-drive leg (catch.mjs:582, client.navigate(handle.frontDoorUrl)) opens a brand-new, unauthenticated Selenium session with zero session carryover from conjure's setup login, and /bookmarks/new is @login_required -> the harness would land on /login/ instead of the bookmark form even if setup somehow succeeded. This generalizes the documenso recipe's already-disclosed 'session-cookie injection ... is the follow-up, not built here' beyond documenso's canvas case to ANY authenticated front door -- which is most of pb's own stated v1 scope ('a signed-in user performs a state-changing action').

front_door.serves: the authenticated 'Add bookmark' form (bookmarks/new.html) -- a single-page, server-rendered form with url/title/description/tags/unread/shared fields. The {marker} placeholder is schema theater (see notes gap 1/3): it is never actually resolved at runtime because the login setup step throws first.

queries.bookmarks: SELECT id, url, shared, unread, owner_id FROM bookmarks_bookmark ORDER BY id DESC;

drive.reason: the 'Add bookmark' front door is a plain server-rendered HTML form (url/title/shared checkbox + Save button) -- a real click/type/click walk, no canvas. Untested beyond conjure: catch.mjs always browser-drives (registry.mjs BROWSER_DRIVE_MODES) and the login-gated front door cannot be reached by that browser session (see notes gap 4).
